subject: Risk-trigger + grace-period buyout request / SLA escalation
messages:
From: Mallory Jensen <mallory.jensen@orionhealth.com>
To: sean.gallagher@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@orionhealth.com, legal@orionhealth.com
Date: 2028-06-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial: Service reliability protections and buyout ask

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Orion’s engineering and procurement teams are aligned on Redwood’s performance, but our risk committee requires stronger contractual remedies for this class of workload (patient-facing decision support). Two concrete asks from our side:

1) A fee-sinking reserve / "buyout" equal to up to 3 months of committed spend that becomes payable if we exercise termination for material SLO failure (we'd like formula and cap).
2) A defined multi-month cure/grace period and a clear, deterministic uptime + latency trigger (e.g., consecutive monthly availability < 99.85% or P99 latency > X ms) that gives us termination rights or cash buyout.

We prefer a capped cash remedy rather than only service credits. Attached is our internal risk policy for context. Can you confirm Redwood can accept a defined buyout construct (with a cap and a cure period)? If not, what alternative escrow/hard-cap options can you offer?

Mallory
Mallory Jensen
Head of Cloud Procurement, Orion Health
--- Attachment: Orion_Risk_Policy_v3.pdf (pdf, 1 page)

From: sean.gallagher@redwood.com
To: Mallory Jensen <mallory.jensen@orionhealth.com>
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-26T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial: Service reliability protections and buyout ask

Mallory —

Appreciate the clarity and the policy doc. Short answer: we can structure a capped cash buyout plus a cure window, but there are a few details we need to align on so the mechanics are objective and operationally enforceable (we avoid ambiguous metrics that block automation). Proposed trade-offs from our side:

- Cure window: 30 days from notice for first occurrence, 14 days for repeat within 6 months.
- Trigger definition: two consecutive calendar months where availability (customer-facing endpoints) < 99.8% or P99 generation latency > 1.5s for the same model/route.
- Cash buyout cap: equal to 3x the monthly committed spend (MRC) for the account, payable upon termination; alternatively, we can offer 1.5x MRC as an immediate cash buyout + remaining credited against future usage.
- We are comfortable with a deterministic formula; we ask to limit termination rights to material, persistent failures and to allow for force majeure/region-wide outages.

I can draft a redline with concrete numbers and the calculation spreadsheet so you can run scenarios. Does Orion have a preferred definition for P99 (backend vs user-observed)? That will change where we measure latency.

I'll loop in Aditya and Marissa (pricing/legal touchpoints) internally to prep a formal counter.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0199

From: sean.gallagher@redwood.com
To: aditya.rao@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-26T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Orion risk policy + buyout ask — need inputs

Team — forwarding Mallory's ask. Quick points we need to decide:

1) Acceptable cap: do we want to offer 3x MRC or 1.5x with hybrid credit? Pricing prefers lower cash exposure; legal needs clean termination mechanics.
2) Metrics: Orion asked for availability and a latency threshold. Engineering: is P99 user-observed feasible, or must we measure at the edge?
3) Cure mechanics: propose 30/14 day step-down. Sales wants a firm buyout option to close the deal.

Aditya, can you confirm where we can measure latency reliably and whether a 1.5s P99 threshold is realistic across their models and our dedicated routing?
Marissa/Rishi, any constraints on cash caps and approval routing if we commit to 3x MRC?

Thanks,
—Sean

From: aditya.rao@redwood.com
To: sean.gallagher@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-28T10:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Orion risk policy + buyout ask — latency & measurement

Sean — quick engineering note:

- We can measure P99 in two places: (A) user-observed (end-to-end) which includes networking variances, or (B) service-side (our entrypoint to model response). For contracts we prefer (B) because it's deterministic. If Orion insists on user-observed, we need a joint measurement plan and probably a dedicated probe network (adds cost).
- 1.5s P99 is reasonable for the 8k-token jobs we've discussed on Dedicated (with warm cache). For mixed, unpredictable workloads, we should use 2.0s. Suggest offering a tiered threshold: 1.5s for pinned dedicated pools + 2.0s for burstable pools.

I'll attach a short worksheet with cost delta for dedicated vs burstable thresholds.

—Aditya

From: sean.gallagher@redwood.com
To: Mallory Jensen <mallory.jensen@orionhealth.com>
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-01T10:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Risk-trigger + grace-period buyout request — Redwood counterproposal

Mallory — thanks for your patience. Attached is a proposed counter that balances Orion’s risk appetite with operational realities. Highlights: 

- Trigger: Two consecutive calendar months where either (i) availability < 99.80% measured at Redwood’s ingress for the contracted route, or (ii) service-side P99 latency > 1.5s for pinned Dedicated pools (2.0s for burstable).
- Cure window: 30 days for first occurrence (from notice), 14 days for any recurrence within 6 months. We will provide a remediation plan and weekly updates during the cure period.
- Cash buyout: Capped at 2x MRC payable if Orion elects termination after cure failure. Alternatively, Orion can elect an immediate buyout equal to 1.5x MRC and terminate without the extended cure.
- Service credits: If Orion elects credits instead of buyout, credits equal to 25% of MRC per impacted month (pro-rated).
- Exclusions: region-level outages, third-party provider failures, and agreed maintenance windows.

Attached: SLA_draft_redline_20280701.pdf and buyout-calculation.xlsx (spreadsheet shows how 2x vs 1.5x scenarios look at Orion's committed volumes).

If Oracle (sic) — sorry, if Orion — can accept the framework, we can lock numbers and route a short amendment for signature. We intentionally capped at 2x MRC to limit Redwood's cash exposure while giving Orion a predictable, cash-based remedy.

Regards,
—Sean
--- Attachments: SLA_draft_redline_20280701.pdf, buyout-calculation.xlsx

From: Mallory Jensen <mallory.jensen@orionhealth.com>
To: sean.gallagher@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@orionhealth.com, legal@orionhealth.com
Date: 2028-07-02T08:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Risk-trigger + grace-period buyout request — Redwood counterproposal

Sean — thanks for the counter and the workbook. Two points from Orion legal/procurement: 

1) The trigger measured at Redwood ingress is not acceptable for us; we need user-observed availability or a mutually operated synthetic probe so we can validate. If you cannot accept user-observed measurement, we require third-party verification and a joint thresholds dashboard.
2) 2x MRC is closer, but procurement prefers 3x MRC as a cap for a high-impact clinical use case. If Redwood will accept 3x MRC, Orion will accept the 30/14 cure cadence and the exclusions you listed.

We can sign quickly with those two changes. Otherwise, legal will push for longer cure windows and a broader set of termination triggers.

Mallory

From: sean.gallagher@redwood.com
To: Mallory Jensen <mallory.jensen@orionhealth.com>
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-04T15:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Risk-trigger + grace-period buyout request — final commercial compromise

Mallory — appreciate the straight feedback. After internal review with Legal and Finance, Redwood can agree to the two items you flagged with the following limited bindings: 

1) Measurement: we will accept user-observed availability measured via a mutually-administered synthetic probe network (joint ops dashboard). Probe configuration will be part of the SOW. Measurement will still be anchored to a documented probe spec to prevent accidental measurement skew.

2) Cash cap: Redwood will accept a cash buyout cap of 3x MRC but with a quarterly aggregate cap for the account: any cash buyouts in a rolling 12-month period are capped at 6x MRC (so multiple buyouts are limited). This preserves predictability for both sides.

Other terms remain as in our 7/1 counter: 30/14 day cure cadence, two consecutive calendar months trigger, P99 thresholds (1.5s dedicated, 2.0s burstable), and exclusions for region-wide outages/force majeure.

If that meets Orion’s risk committee, I’ll push a one-page amendment to Legal for signature and we can attach to the MSA.

Thanks — looking forward to closing.

—Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com
